proof:
# Exact nonconvexity at the proposed fractional-packing threshold

This certificate disproves convexity, and even lattice-midpoint convexity, of the fractional-packing superlevel region at t=M/2^n. It does not disprove existence of some center meeting that threshold.

Let the planar house pentagon have vertices

A=(0,0), B=(4,0), C=(4,4), D=(2,6), E=(0,4).

Let R=conv{A,B,C,D,E}. Its lattice points are: all25 points (x,y) with x=0,...,4 and y=0,...,4; the three points (1,5),(2,5),(3,5); and (2,6). Thus there are exactly29.

Take n=3 and

P=(R x [0,1]) intersect Z^3.

This is a finite lattice-convex set of58 points. Give its five bottom-layer vertices (A,0),...,(E,0) weight one. Give the other24 bottom-layer points weight1/2400 each. Give every one of the29 top-layer points weight1099/2900. All weights are strictly positive, their total is

M=5+24/2400+29(1099/2900)=5+1/100+1099/100=16,

and every weight is at most one, strictly below M/2^3=2.

Let

p=(3,3,0), q=(1,3,0), m=(2,3,0)=(p+q)/2.

All three points belong to P, and p,q have the same parity.

At p, the two disjoint pairs {(A,0),(C,0)} and {(B,0),(D,0)} both have p in their segments:

p=(1/4)(A,0)+(3/4)(C,0)
 =(1/2)(B,0)+(1/2)(D,0).

Packing each pair with value one gives f(p)>=2.

At q, the two disjoint pairs {(A,0),(D,0)} and {(B,0),(E,0)} both contain q:

q=(1/2)(A,0)+(1/2)(D,0)
 =(1/4)(B,0)+(3/4)(E,0).

Thus f(q)>=2.

The midpoint m lies on no segment joining two of the five planar vertices. For a completely arithmetic certificate, the signed planar determinants det(V_i-m,V_j-m), ordered as AB,AC,AD,AE,BC,BD,BE,CD,CE,DE, are respectively

12,4,-6,-8,8,6,-4,6,4,6,

all nonzero.

Define dual costs t_v by assigning1/3 to each of the five bottom vertices, one to every other bottom point, and zero to every top point. These costs are feasible for the packing LP at m. Any convex representation of a point with third coordinate zero uses only bottom-layer points with positive coefficients. Hence any qualifying group contains a bottom-layer subgroup whose convex hull contains m. If the group contains a nonvertex bottom point, its dual cost is already at least one. Otherwise it must contain at least three of the five bottom vertices, since m lies on none of their pair segments; their dual cost is at least one.

The dual objective is

5/3+24/2400=5/3+1/100=503/300<2.

Therefore f(m)<=503/300<2=M/2^3, while f(p),f(q)>=2. The superlevel set {z in R^3:f(z)>=M/2^3} is nonconvex and its intersection with the lattice is not closed under integer midpoint formation.

The weights here are arbitrary positive source weights, as allowed by the independent packing question. No assertion is made that this particular weight table is the fiber-volume table of a convex body.
